findings.title: Device limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert (TOCTOU)
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice first runs CountDevices and then does a separate INSERT. Concurrent requests from many new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Under load, which is when the limit matters, it is not enforced. The count and insert need to be atomic, for example one conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit, or a transaction.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from async goroutine to synchronous DB work on the auth path
findings.body: The previous implementation tagged the device in a background goroutine with a timeout and panic recovery. TagDevice now runs inline in Authenticate with the request context. Every anonymous request that misses the local cache now blocks on a COUNT query plus an INSERT or UPDATE, which adds latency. A DB slowdown or an expired request context also stalls or fails anonymous auth. The panic recovery was dropped as well.

findings.title: Local cache is populated before the DB write, so rejected devices are cached as tagged
findings.body: tagDeviceUI calls localCache.SetDefault(key) before CreateOrUpdateDevice. If the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached or any other DB error, the key stays cached for 29 minutes. Subsequent requests from that device return nil from the cache and are authenticated as anonymous. The limit is therefore bypassed after the first rejection: only the first request is denied and later ones are let through. The key should be cached only after a successful write.

findings.title: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-rows-affected result
findings.body: A zero-row result is reported as limit reached. On MySQL, RowsAffected returns 0 when the row values are unchanged, because the default driver does not use CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS. An existing device that is re-tagged at the limit with an identical client_ip, user_agent and updated_at second would then be wrongly rejected. The WHERE clause also excludes devices older than 30 days, so a known device that has been idle is rejected as new.

findings.title: Args slice mutated inside the session callback
findings.body: In updateDevice and CreateOrUpdateDevice, `args = append([]any{query}, args...)` reassigns the outer variable inside the closure. If WithDbSession retries the callback, the query gets prepended twice and the Exec call is malformed. Building a local slice inside the closure would avoid this.

findings.title: Limited test coverage for device limit
findings.body: The test only covers a new device being rejected at the limit. It does not cover an existing device still being updatable at the limit, a device older than 30 days being rejected, or the limit disabled with 0 (apart from the incidental use in other tests). There is also no test for the client.go path that now returns the error from Authenticate, and no test for the setting parsing.

findings.title: New device_limit setting is undocumented
findings.body: The new `[auth.anonymous] device_limit` option is not added to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini or the docs. The PR description is also an empty template. Users cannot discover the option or its semantics, such as 0 meaning unlimited.
